question.text: Avanti Buyout Fund (Cat II) acquired investee Takshila Logistics for equity cheque of INR 100 crore in Year 0. At exit in Year 5, equity proceeds are INR 300 crore. What is the gross IRR (no intermediate dividends)?

explanation.text: The Logic: IRR = (Exit / Entry)^(1/n) - 1 = (300/100)^(1/5) - 1 = 3^0.2 - 1 = 1.2457 - 1 = 24.57% ~ 24.6%. The MOIC is 3.0x over 5 years. The Trap: 20% is the simple average return (3x - 1 = 200% / 5 years / 2 = wrong logic); 25% is a rounded approximation commonly cited; 15% understates. Always use the geometric (compounded) IRR for PE exit math. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A (Distributor) also tests IRR. XIX-C covers the same. XXI-B's twrR (time-weighted) is inappropriate for PE — MOIC and IRR are the PE standards because of the J-curve and irregular drawdowns.
